sources.citation: Pinart, Alphonse L. 1900. Notes sur les tribus indiennes de famille guarano-guaymies de l'isthme de Panama et du Centre-Amérique. (Newberry Library Ayer 1471 G91 P64 1900)
sources.note: Ethnographic/classificatory notes (Dorasque-Changuina family, tribal locations) plus a short comparative wordlist with a DORASQUE column; no remarks on pronunciation or accent.

sources.citation: Franco, Blas José [c.1792], ed. Alphonse L. Pinart. 1882. Noticia de los indios guaymies y de sus costumbres [with] Vocabulario de las lenguas guaymi sabanero y dorasque. San Francisco: A. L. Pinart. (Glottolog: Pinart 1882, Noticias de los indios del Departamento de Veragua)
sources.note: 18th-century missionary wordlist (Dorasque = Gualaca column, from p. 50), printed with the manuscript's orthography unchanged (preface: 'Je n'ai pas cru devoir changer ni l'orthographe ni la phraséologie du texte'). Some Dorasque forms carry a Spanish acute accent (Gdaapá '8', Gdatabóco '10', Queréle 'sol', Viuú 'estrella', Gdaderegúe, Datigá), but no note on pronunciation or accent placement anywhere.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page dora1242 (refs: Pinart 1882, Miranda de Cabal 1974, Pinart 1890, Constenla Umaña 1985, Gómez Moreno 1997; hh.bib copy in
sources.note: Lists five references, none typed grammar/phonology; the language is marked extinct (last speaker reported 1882 by Pinart; survivals into the 20th century per Torres de Araúz 1980).

sources.citation: Pache, Matthias J. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan historical linguistics. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (hdl 1887/67094), front matter 'Data presentation' pp. xv-xvi
sources.note: States that pre-modern data such as Pinart's (1890) Chánguena/Dorasque forms are cited only as graphemic representations in pointed brackets (e.g. <báli> 'salt, sea', Pinart 1890: 21, 29); no statement about Dorasque stress. The full text and chapters could not be downloaded (repository served an access-blocked page after the first file).

sources.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo. 1985. Las lenguas dorasque y chánguena y sus relaciones genealógicas. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 11(2): 81-91. DOI 10.15517/rfl.v11i2.16685
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory article (lexicostatistics, sound correspondences, Proto-Chibchan reflexes). Describes the only surviving materials (Pinart 1890: Chumulu 431 items, Gualaca 421, Chánguena 134; Miranda de Cabal 1974: ~700 words + 500 phrases from a semi-speaker) and calls their transcription 'problemática'. Cites Pinart's accent-marked spellings (xatú, báliga, sivó, duquí) but says nothing about stress or accent; a full-text search for stress/accent acent/tónic/sílab/prosod/tono gives no hits.

sources.citation: Pinart, Alphonse L. 1890. Vocabulario castellano-dorasque: dialectos chumulu, gualaca y changuina. Paris: Leroux (Petite Bibliothèque Américaine II), 42 pp.
sources.note: The main primary corpus (Chumulu, Gualaca, Chánguena); its front matter may carry an orthographic note on accents, and its accent-marked forms are the only stress evidence that exists.

sources.citation: Pinart, Alphonse L. 1882. Noticias de los indios del Departamento de Veragua, y vocabularios de las lenguas guaymi, norteño, sabanero y dorasque. San Francisco: Bancroft. (Google scan of the same 1882 edition)
sources.note: Same text as the Franco/Pinart item (poorer scanned); no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo. 2011. Estado de conservación y documentación de las lenguas de América Central pertenecientes a las agrupaciones jicaque, lenca, misumalpa, chibchense y chocó. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 37(1): 135-195.
sources.note: First-hand documentation-status survey by the leading Chibchanist. For Dorasque it inventories the four data sources and states that NO phonological analysis of the data has ever been carried out (so no phonemic system, and a fortiori no statement on tone or accent, exists in the literature); the summary table (p. 150) lists for Dorasque only 'ordenamiento del vocabulario por campos semánticos' under analyses done, versus 'sistema fonemático' for e.g. Cacaopera and Huetar. It makes no claim about whether Dorasque had tone. Useful as the authoritative citation that the tone/stress of Dorasque…

tone.quote: En el caso del dorasque, se dispone de cuatro fuentes de datos: Juan Franco (última década del siglo XVIII), unos 465 vocablos; Pinart (1890), 431 vocablos de la variedad chumulu y 421 de la variedad gualaca; Miranda de Cabal (1974), 700 palabras y 500 frases cortas, y Gómez Moreno (1997), las traducciones al dorasque de 150 palabras y frases en castellano. Gómez Moreno realizó un ordenamiento de los materiales disponibles por campos semánticos. No se ha llevado a cabo un análisis fonológico de los datos, ni se han ordenado los elementos léxicos en orden alfabético.
tone.translation: In the case of Dorasque, four data sources are available: Juan Franco (last decade of the 18th century), about 465 words; Pinart (1890), 431 words of the Chumulu variety and 421 of the Gualaca variety; Miranda de Cabal (1974), 700 words and 500 short phrases; and Gómez Moreno (1997), the Dorasque translations of 150 Spanish words and phrases. Gómez Moreno arranged the available materials by semantic field. No phonological analysis of the data has been carried out, nor have the lexical items been put in alphabetical order.
